user_input: I've been staring at my phone for three hours now. My entire hostel wing went to Gokarna for the long weekend, and I’m sitting here in this damp room trying to debug a binary tree assignment that won't compile. Every story on my feed is them laughing, drinking, and having the time of their lives while I couldn't even afford the trip budget because of my backlog fees. I feel like an absolute ghost who could disappear from this campus and nobody would even notice.

Every time I open LinkedIn, it's like a punch in the gut. Another batchmate posting their 'I'm thrilled to share I've secured a 15 LPA offer at...' while my CGPA is a pathetic 6.8 and I can't even get past the first round of coding tests. My parents call me every Sunday asking when I'll get placed like the neighbor's kid, and I just end up scrolling through these success posts feeling completely paralyzed. I feel so small and useless, like I'm already a failure before my life has even started.

I forgot to mute the wing group chat, and today my phone just kept buzzing with pictures of them eating at the new cafe down the road. They didn't even ask if I wanted to come, even though they know I've been stuck in my room with a fever all week. I'm just sitting here eating instant noodles, watching their WhatsApp status updates of them clinking glasses and laughing. It's like I'm completely invisible to them unless they need to copy my lab records.

Valentine's week is the absolute worst. My Instagram feed is literally overflowing with couples holding hands on the campus lawns, posting long cheesy paragraphs, and going on dates. I’ve spent the last four hours swiping through these stories in my dark hostel room, feeling this physical ache in my chest because I've never been loved like that. I feel so ugly and unlovable, like there’s something fundamentally broken inside me that keeps everyone at a distance.

During Diwali vacation, everyone went back home and their Snapchat maps are just filled with family photos, sweets, and traditional clothes. I couldn't go back because my train tickets got waitlisted and flight prices were insane, so I'm stuck alone in this empty hostel building with only the security guard outside. Watching my school friends reunite on social media while I sit in this dead silence makes me feel like I don't belong anywhere anymore. I feel completely abandoned by the world.

It’s 2 AM and I’ve been scrolling through Instagram for three hours. Everyone from my branch is at some weekend beach trip in Gokarna, posting these stupid, perfect reels with aesthetic sunset filters. Meanwhile, I'm stuck in my cramped hostel room, staring at my DSA lab assignment that I can't compile for the life of me, with a 6.2 CGPA and a looming backlog. I feel like an absolute ghost watching everyone else live these colorful, high-package, socially perfect lives while I'm just rotting here.

Every single time I open LinkedIn, my chest gets so tight. It's just endless 'I am thrilled to share...' posts about 40 LPA packages, summer internships at FAANG, and guys from my batch talking about their tech-stack breakthroughs. I haven't even cracked a single aptitude round yet, and seeing their smiling professional headshots makes me want to throw my phone against the wall. I look at my own empty profile and feel this paralyzing sense of failure, like I'm already permanently left behind in life.

I saw the WhatsApp stories today of my school friends back home meeting up for a reunion dinner, laughing and sitting around the same old tea stall we used to love. They didn’t even add me to the planning group, probably because they think I've 'moved on' since coming to this tier-1 college. But I have no one here; I eat every single mess dinner in complete silence while staring at my phone pretending to be busy. Seeing them happy without me makes me feel like I have no home left to go back to, and no place to call mine here.

It's Friday night and my hostel corridor is completely dead because everyone went out to some club or pub in the city. I'm just lying on my bed, mindlessly refreshing my Snapchat map and seeing all their Bitmojis clustered together at these loud, glowing party spots. I didn’t get invited to a single plan, and when I try to post a random aesthetic photo of my laptop setup just to look 'busy' and 'productive' on my story, I feel this disgusting wave of self-hate. I'm literally performing a fake life for people who wouldn't even notice if I disappeared.

My phone buzzes and my heart leaps, thinking someone finally texted me to hang out, but it’s just another automated notification from BeReal or an advertisement. I scroll through our batch WhatsApp group and see them sharing inside jokes about the DBMS midterms, using terms and memes I don't even understand because I'm not in any of their close circles. I feel like an absolute spectator in my own youth, watching everyone else form these effortless bonds through screens while I'm locked inside this silent room, slowly going numb.

I’ve been scrolling through my class WhatsApp stories for two hours. Everyone is out at that new cafe celebrating the end of DSA midterms, laughing, posting group selfies with 'the gang' tags. I’m sitting here in my 8x8 hostel room with a cold plate of mess food, trying to clear my backlog from last semester, feeling like I’m completely invisible to them. If I disappeared tomorrow, I don't think my name would even register in their group chats.

Every time I open LinkedIn, my feed is just loaded with 'I am thrilled to share that I have secured an SDE internship at...' posts from my batchmates. My parents keep sending me screenshots of these updates asking why my CGPA is stuck at 6.8 and why I haven't cracked any placement drives yet. It’s like everyone has figured out how to win at life while I’m just stuck in this endless loop of failure, completely cut off from the rest of the world.

It's the long weekend and my entire Instagram feed is flooded with pictures of my wingmates trekking in the hills. They made a separate group chat to plan the whole trip and didn't even bother to ask me if I wanted to join, even though they see me everyday in the corridor. I'm just sitting here watching their stories over and over, feeling this heavy, hollow ache in my chest like I'm a ghost haunting my own hostel room.

I just saw forty different WhatsApp status updates wishing this one guy in our batch a happy birthday with paragraphs of inside jokes and memories. On my birthday last month, I didn't get a single post, not even a message on the main class group. I spent the whole night scrolling through social media, watching everyone else's tight-knit bonds, and realizing I have spent two years here and haven't made a single deep connection.

I made the mistake of looking at my high school friends' holiday posts on Instagram today. They all look so happy at their new universities, making new best friends, going to parties, and I’m just sitting here drowning in midterms and lab reports, completely isolated. I tried to text our old group chat but the replies were so dry and formal; it’s like social media is showing me in real-time how easily I was replaced and forgotten.

Scrolling Instagram and seeing everyone from my DSA batch post pictures from their weekend getaway to the hills while I was stuck in my room failing compilation tests. I've spent the last three hours refreshing their stories, watching them laugh, and looking at my blank VS Code screen. It feels like everyone got a handbook on how to make friends in college except me, and I'm just watching their perfect lives through a glass screen.

My LinkedIn feed is literally killing me. Every second post is 'I am thrilled to share that I've secured an internship at FAANG' or some 9.8 CGPA senior bragging about their package. I look at my 6.2 CGPA, my empty inbox, and then I check my WhatsApp where the college group chat has 200+ unread messages of people planning parties I wasn't invited to. I just put my phone on silent, buried my head in my pillow, and wondered why I'm even alive if I'm this invisible.

It was my birthday yesterday. I spent the whole day checking my phone, hoping for some stories or long paragraphs like the ones my classmates post for each other with college aesthetic collages. I got exactly three dry 'HBD' texts on the hostel wing group. Seeing everyone else's elaborate birthday bash posts on Snapchat makes me feel like if I packed my bags and left this campus tomorrow, not a single person would even notice my absence.

Every time I open Instagram, I see my school friends hanging out with their new college groups, putting up stories with inside jokes. Meanwhile, I'm sitting in this stuffy double-sharing hostel room, my roommate hasn't spoken to me in three days, and I'm eating cold maggi alone. Social media makes me feel like I’m the only one who failed the transition to college life, like I'm frozen in time while everyone else moved on.

I spent my whole weekend scrolling through WhatsApp status updates of my batchmates at the cultural fest. I didn't go because my social anxiety was spiking, but now looking at their group photos makes my chest physically ache. It's this toxic loop where I'm too scared to join them, but seeing them happy online just confirms my worst fear—that I’m completely disposable and easily replaced.

Just spent three hours scrolling Instagram reels and stories, and I honestly feel sick to my stomach. Why does it feel like there’s this massive, vibrant party happening in the world, and I’m the only one who didn't get an invite? I don't even know how to talk to these people on Monday anymore.
